chapter: Sarah Vaughan and the Basie band
title: What makes the magic: Ellington's answer about 18 men
summary: Jones cannot analyze why some nights are better; he cites Ellington's remark that musicians sometimes just do not feel like playing.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you ever try to analyze what makes the magic happen some nights, when it gets greater than ever? What it is, what the chemistry is, what combination?
I've tried to analyze it, and I can't figure it out.

Yeah. Something just comes off, you know? And we don't know, normally. I think that Ellington had an answer once. You know, he was never lost for words anyway. And some guy asked him, said, 'Well, Duke, don't you -- aren't you concerned about the discipline or the band sounding one way or the other way?' And Duke says, 'Well, this is 18 men trying to make a living. Some nights they just don't feel like playing.' But it's never bad. It might -- you know, it was never bad. Just that some nights they were just better.

You know? And I think that was a very logical answer, because -- oh, Duke, gee whiz, or even with the Stuff Smith Trio with John Levy, in that situation. Sometimes we would -- we would be pretty hot. Sometimes we would sound --
